# Privacy Documented Beside The Feature

The privacy argument is not filed in one policy document — it is **restated at every site where the
sensitive thing happens**: in the vision doc, in the legal chapter, in the install guide, in the SRS
non-functional requirements, and in the header comment of the source file that does the capture.

In [[farely]] the same two invariants — never tap Accept, never come between the driver and an identity
check — are written down in at least six places, in two languages of expression (prose and code
comment) and two programming languages.

## Evidence

The trade-off is stated where the trade-off is made:

> "This is a deliberate, documented departure from \"nothing leaves the phone\": a screen capture
> leaves the device **only** for this classifier, and only for screens that pass a cheap on-device
> novelty gate."
> — Farley/docs/VISION.md, 2026-07-13

And restated as a comment on the keyword list that enforces it:

> "Deliberately excludes verification/selfie terms: identity checks are detected on-device by the
> coordinator and NEVER routed to cloud vision."
> — Farley/apps/android/.../FarelyAccessibilityService.kt, 2026-07-13

The second quote is the pattern in one line. A developer editing `NOVELTY_HINTS` to add a keyword reads
the rule at the moment they could break it. A privacy policy in a separate repository would not have
been in that field of view — which is worth noting given that
[[privacy-policy-template]] exists and, by chronology, covers neither of the author's two products.

## Why the redundancy is the point

It is the [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] habit applied to a legal and ethical constraint
rather than to a data field. Six copies is normally a maintenance smell; here each copy sits next to a
different way of violating the rule, so the duplication tracks the attack surface rather than the
document tree. The ToS and ban-risk warning is likewise repeated four times — README warning block,
VISION §7, the legal chapter (including a draft in-app disclaimer), and SRS NFR-L-1.

## The two costs, both visible in this repo

**Copies drift.** The 2026-07-24 README rewrite for public release restated the privacy claim as "runs
fully on-device", which is **less** accurate than the VISION text it echoed: map tiles and
fueleconomy.gov are unconditional outbound calls, and the [[anthropic-messages-api]] path ships in the
bundle. Six sites of truth means six chances to write the sixth one carelessly — see
[[documentation-drift]] and [[on-device-first-inference]].

**Documentation is not enforcement.** The identity-check freeze is corroborated in three independent
mechanisms, but all three are keyword heuristics; a verification screen containing an unlisted novelty
word could still be captured. The docs assert a guarantee the code makes only probable. Stating the
rule six times does not make it structural — see [[opt-in-cloud-fallback]] and
[[never-automate-the-accept-tap]], where the boundary *is* structural and the difference is instructive.
